summary: Teams of 2-4 students create a website celebrating unsung heroes in their local community, including a landing page and at least three themed sub-pages. Teams submit their website and required documentation before the deadline, then present their project to judges at the competition. The event evaluates both the technical quality of the website and the team's presentation skills.
time_limits: No more than three (3) minutes for setup
No more than five (5) minutes for the presentation
No more than five (5) minutes for judges’ questions
Presentation will be stopped at five (5) minutes
submission_requirements: Submit clickable Project URL (with login credentials if needed), Works Cited formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual, BPA Release Form(s) and AI Usage and Documentation Form in one combined PDF
Team ID is required for all submissions
Materials from non-registered contestants and/or those missing Team ID cannot be accepted
Materials must follow the organization’s BPA Graphic Standards and make proper use of the BPA logo and/or organization’s name
what_to_bring: One single-sided laptop, notebook, or tablet for their presentation
competencies: Design and develop a responsive, accessible website optimized for cross-browser compatibility
Apply leadership skills and collaborate on web development projects
Apply ethical standards, copyright compliance, and data privacy principles in all aspects of web design and content management
Apply problem-solving and troubleshooting techniques to resolve technical challenges and ensure secure, efficient web functionality
Proofread to ensure content accuracy and clarity

rubric.criterion: Team followed Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

Team submitted clickable Project URL (with login credentials if needed), Works Cited formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual, BPA Release Form(s) and AI Usage and Documentation Form in one combined PDF.

rubric.description: Visual organization is clear and intuitive; colors and fonts are highly aesthetic and enhance readability; consistent format is maintained across all pages.
Graphics strongly enhance the topic; highly creative and original design using templates, code, or both.
The website demonstrates a good understanding of the topic and presents relevant and accurate information throughout.

Website works seamlessly across browsers; source code is clean, organized, and validated; innovative technologies (e.g., SASS, Python, JavaScript) are effectively used; grammar and spelling are flawless.
All links present, fully functional, consistently formatted; navigation path is clear, logical, and easy to follow.

rubric.criterion: Team followed Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

rubric.description: Team maintains good eye contact, uses appropriate gestures and body language, and vary their tone and pace adequately.
Presentation content flows adequately, and each team contestant’s role is clear and integrated into the presentation. Transitions between speakers and/or points are smooth.
Presentation demonstrates a good understanding of the topic and includes relevant and accurate information.
Responses are detailed, insightful, and effectively address the judges’ questions.
Setup lasted no longer than three (3) minutes and presentation lasted no more than five (5) minutes.
At least two original team members were present during the presentation.

judging_notes: AI Policy Level 2 Permitted with Citation
Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the team and must take place within the time allotted
No Internet access will be provided on-site at NLC; however, teams may provide their own access to be used only for their presentation to the judges
Finals may be part of the competition
Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring
eligibility_notes: Any middle level contestant may enter this judged team event
A team will consist of 2-4 contestants
Teams must be registered for the national competition before the submission deadline and compete in both parts of the event to be ranked
Entries that do not follow the provided topic or the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines or Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy will be disqualified
Each state is allowed three (3) entries
